classification.difficultyReason: Organise predictions in a table, then combine five at-least-one-correct constraints to deduce a unique ordering.

content.prompt: Five boys made paper gliders and were arguing about which would fly furthest, so they decided to have a competition. Adrian said his glider would come first and Jonathon’s would come second. Lars said his would win, Khan’s would come second and Rory’s fifth. Khan thought his glider would come third, and that Jonathon’s would be last. Jonathon said Rory’s would come third and Adrian’s fourth. Rory thought Lars’s glider would be second-last.

inlines.text: Use the above information to complete the table below.

answer.worked: Place each predicted competitor in the column for the predicted placing, using the row of the boy making the prediction. Adrian: Adrian 1st, Jonathon 2nd. Jonathon: Rory 3rd, Adrian 4th. Khan: Khan 3rd, Jonathon 5th. Lars: Lars 1st, Khan 2nd, Rory 5th. Rory: Lars 4th. Leave cells blank where no prediction was made.

children.label: b
children.prompt: After the competition, it turned out that each boy had made at least one correct prediction. Determine the placings.

inlines.text: Start with Rory’s sole prediction, then eliminate predictions that conflict with the placings already determined.
Rory made only one prediction, so Lars must be 4th.
Adrian cannot also be 4th. Therefore Jonathon’s correct prediction must be Rory 3rd.
Khan cannot also be 3rd. Therefore Khan’s correct prediction must be Jonathon 5th.
Jonathon cannot also be 2nd. Therefore Adrian’s correct prediction must be Adrian 1st.
The remaining place is 2nd, so Khan is 2nd. This also makes Lars’s prediction of Khan 2nd correct.
The placings are Adrian 1st, Khan 2nd, Rory 3rd, Lars 4th and Jonathon 5th. Every boy has at least one correct prediction.
